author: byungilm
title: Windows CC build fails with compiler/linker out-of-memory errors under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode
failed_jobs.symptom: cl.exe fatal error C1060 (compiler out of heap space) on multiple template functional test TUs, followed by link.exe fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) building ov_api_conformance_tests.exe

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status-check job failed because the upstream Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode job failed

key_errors:
FAILED: build-modules/template/tests/functional/CMakeFiles/ov_template_func_tests.dir/Release/op_reference/ctc_greedy_decoder.cpp.obj
C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\openvino\thirdparty\gtest\gtest\googletest\include\gtest/gtest_pred_impl.h(252): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space

FAILED: build-modules/template/tests/functional/CMakeFiles/ov_template_func_tests.dir/Release/op_reference/cos.cpp.obj
C:\BuildTools\VC\Tools\MSVC\14.42.34433\include\memory(1641): fatal error C1060: compiler is out of heap space

root_cause: The Windows CC (Conditional Compilation) Release build compiles with CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31 on a shared/constrained Windows runner. Under this parallelism, multiple cl.exe worker processes compete for address space/heap simultaneously, causing MSVC's cl.exe to run out of heap space (C1060) on several unrelated template functional-test translation units (ctc_greedy_decoder.cpp, cos.cpp). Shortly after, the linker (link.exe) building ov_api_conformance_tests.exe also exhausts memory (LNK1102). This is a resource-exhaustion failure on the runner/build-parallelism configuration, not a defect in the merged PR's code change (a GPU-plugin graph-transformation fix unrelated to Windows CC/template tests). The same signature has now recurred 18 times since 2026-11-03, consistently tied to high parallel build concurrency on Windows runners.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside CI; it is a resource-contention issue tied to the Windows CI runner's available memory under CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31. Locally, building the `template` and `conformance` modules with Release config and comparably high `/MP` or ninja parallelism on a memory-constrained Windows machine can reproduce C1060/LNK1102.
recommended_actions: Reduce CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL for the Windows CC Release build job, or switch to a Windows runner SKU with more RAM
Investigate ccache/ninja scheduling to avoid launching too many concurrent cl.exe/link.exe processes relative to available memory
Consider splitting the conformance/template test target builds into separate parallel-limited stages to cap peak memory usage
Escalate to CI infra owners given this signature has now recurred 18 times since 2026-11-03 with no apparent fix in progress
prevention_strategies: Tune build parallelism to the runner's actual memory budget (e.g., derive CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL from available RAM rather than core count) and monitor runner memory usage during Windows CC builds to catch regressions in parallelism/runner-size configuration before they cause recurring post-commit failures.
historical_context: This exact signature (C1060 compiler out-of-heap-space + LNK1102 linker out-of-memory under high parallelism on the Windows CC build) has recurred 18 times since first observed on 2026-11-03T07:07:04Z, most recently a few hours before this run (2026-11-20T09:38:45Z). It is the single most frequent recurring pattern in the post-commit knowledge base and has not been tied to any specific PR's code changes across occurrences - a strong indicator of an infrastructure/configuration issue (build parallelism vs. runner memory) rather than a code regression.
